steps.executor_prompt: Minimize this app, then go to the Google Authenticator app. If there is a Device Pin, enter {device_pin}. Navigate to the main page of Google Authenticator where the OTP can be found: for a mail or messaging app this is the inbox or conversation list, and for an authenticator app this is the list of accounts with their codes. Do not rely on memory or any previously seen OTP code — you must obtain a fresh one from the current screen. If it is the detailed page of a message, go back to the main inbox. If the app shows a list of messages or emails, refresh it (e.g. swipe down from the top), wait 3 seconds for it to load, check the Default Browser and go to accounts.evernote.com/login, then open the newest item at the top and read the OTP code inside it. If the app directly displays rotating codes, find the entry corresponding to Default Browser and go to accounts.evernote.com/login and read its currently displayed code; if that code is about to expire, wait for it to rotate and read the new one. Report that OTP code as your final answer.

Return to the target in the default browser and inspect the current page. Submit a newly rotated code from the matching authenticator entry only into the target's normal six-digit authenticator-code form; never enter it into a backup-code field. If a backup-code page appears, go back to the normal OTP form. If that form is no longer reachable, reopen the target login URL and repeat the complete sign-in using the task-provided username and password, then obtain and immediately submit another fresh authenticator code. Reinspect controls after every navigation instead of reusing element indices. Report success only when the exact target displays authenticated account content or an explicit login-success confirmation.
